=== README.md ===
# Agent sandbox

Agent sandbox is a Nix-built container service for running coding-agent workloads as an unprivileged user. This bootstrap provides the Rust service package, OCI image, rootless Podman environment, Docker Compose compatibility, and an ephemeral `systemd-nspawn` runner.

The service currently exposes `GET /healthz` on port 8080. The filesystem and command RPC planes described in [INSTRUCTIONS.md](INSTRUCTIONS.md) are the next implementation milestone.

## Set up

Install Nix with flakes enabled. Enter the development environment:

```console
nix develop
```

The first shell activation after each reboot asks for wheel authorization. It installs a cgroup delegation drop-in under `/run`, then starts a rootless, Docker-compatible Podman API as the transient `agent-sandbox-podman.service` user unit. The service lasts for the user session; neither the drop-in nor its marker survives a reboot. Set `AGENT_SANDBOX_SKIP_PODMAN_SERVICE=1` on hosts where service startup is not wanted.

With nix-direnv installed, `direnv allow` activates the same shell when entering the repository. The shell includes Cargo, Clippy, rustfmt, Podman, and podman-compose and exports `DOCKER_HOST` and `DOCKER_SOCK` for the rootless Podman socket.

## Build and check

```console
nix fmt
nix flake check --print-build-logs
nix build .#agent-sandbox
nix build .#agent-image
```

The root flake follows the consumer-clean structure from `nix-project-template`: package and image definitions live under `nix/flake/`, while formatters, hooks, and shell tools are isolated in `dev/`.

## Run containers

Load the Nix-built OCI archive into Podman:

```console
podman load < "$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths .#agent-image)"
podman run --rm --publish 8080:8080 ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest
```

The compatibility Dockerfile and Compose definition run through rootless Podman:

```console
podman-compose up --build
podman-compose down
```

Both images run as `sandbox-manager`, use `/home/user` as the home and working directory, preinstall the Python libraries declared in `pyproject.toml`, and start `agent-sandbox` as their entrypoint. `uv.lock` pins the compatibility Dockerfile's complete Python environment. Compose references `ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest`; `--build` replaces it locally with the compatibility Dockerfile build.

## Continuous integration

GitHub Actions remains a check-only adapter. SourceHut runs the same `nix flake check --print-build-logs` contract from [`.build.yml`](.build.yml), builds the Nix OCI archive, and publishes only `refs/heads/main` to GHCR. Other SourceHut branches build and test the image but cannot publish it.

The SourceHut repository is the registered private mirror at `git.sr.ht/~fuzzybear3965/agent-sandbox`. A push containing `.build.yml` submits a build automatically. The manifest uses the existing SourceHut CI SSH-key secret to clone this private repository.

### GHCR secret

Create a GitHub personal access token (classic) for `johnrichardrinehart` at <https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=write:packages>. This URL avoids the GitHub token form's default addition of the broad `repo` scope. Keep only `write:packages`, which includes image download and upload; do not add `repo`, `workflow`, or `delete:packages`.

The SourceHut file secret declared in `.build.yml` is mounted at `~/.ghcr_pat`; its complete contents are the token. SourceHut runs tasks with shell tracing enabled, so the publishing app reads the file with tracing disabled and passes the token to `skopeo login` through standard input.

A main build publishes `ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest` and `0.0.n`, where `n` is the main commit count, then confirms that both tags have the same digest. GHCR makes a new personal package private by default. After its first publication, change the package visibility to public in its GitHub package settings so the documented Compose command can pull it without authentication.

## Run with systemd-nspawn

```console
nix run .#agent-systemd-nspawn
```

This command asks for wheel authorization and launches the Nix root filesystem through `systemd-nspawn` with an ephemeral overlay. It runs the service as `sandbox-manager`; changes vanish when the unit exits. Inspect the generated command without elevation with:

```console
nix run .#agent-systemd-nspawn -- --dry-run
```
=== AGENTS.md ===
# Project agent instructions

## Immutable files

- Do not modify `INSTRUCTIONS.md`. Preserve its exact contents and hash across every revision.

## CI monitoring

- Push every `main` update to both `origin` (GitHub) and `fork` (SourceHut). Pushing only to `origin` does not trigger the SourceHut build.
- Limit each wait for a queued CI run to 30 seconds unless the run starts or otherwise makes progress.
- When GitHub has no available runner, record the run ID, status, and URL, then continue independent work instead of polling indefinitely.
- Recheck pending runs after other work completes.

content.text:
Record a canonicalization change without treating it as a repository move.

Use this when the old source was archived, source-closed, deleted, or otherwise stopped being the canonical source, and development resumed under a different organization or repository. Successors are metadata only: they do not move the old checkout, do not create alias symlinks, and do not merge the old and new repository records.

Use `repo move` instead for a rename, transfer, or locator change of the same hosted repository.

Usage: repo successor [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  set  Record canonical source continuation without treating it as a move

Options:
      --dir <DIR>
          Run repository-context commands as if started from DIR

      --json
          Print command results as machine-readable JSON

Finish agent-sandbox under ./INSTRUCTIONS.md: preserve the completed bootstrap, CI pivot, reviewed merge, and publication flow; implement a single-stage Nix compatibility Dockerfile; then publish and audit the update.

- Preserve the root flake, Nix OCI image, Rust binary and lock files, rootless Podman/podman-compose devShell, session-long transient Docker-compatible Podman service with wheel authorization, Compose compatibility, and `nix run .#agent-systemd-nspawn`.

- Build the Rust service through the locked project flake. Supply Python, every library in `requirements.txt`, Tesseract, and certificates through one reusable Nix runtime environment. Do not use a Python base, `apt`, `pip`, or another Docker stage.
- Preserve runtime UID/GID 10001 and user `sandbox-manager`, `/home/user`, entrypoint, port 8080, health check, and rootless Podman/Compose operation. Keep only required source/build state where safe while retaining the Nix runtime closure.

- Preserve the public GitHub successor and repo-manager successor relationship. Keep all public Git objects sanitized of the prior organization/domain, variants, misspellings, and affiliated identities; retain Acme replacement metadata and removed unsafe signatures.
- Preserve the original bootstrap commit’s Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, `fn main()`, and Nix foundation.
- Keep GitHub Actions check-only with no GHCR authority.
- Keep `git.sr.ht/~fuzzybear3965/agent-sandbox` a private repo-managed mirror of canonical `github.com/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox`; use only mirror-owned managed worktrees and registered remotes for SourceHut pushes.
- Preserve `.build.yml`: authoritative Nix checks, Nix OCI build, and publication only from `main` as GHCR `latest` plus deterministic `0.0.n`, where n is main’s commit count. Non-main builds must not publish.
- Use the declared SourceHut clone-key and GHCR file secrets. The `johnrichardrinehart` classic PAT’s temporary `repo, write:packages` scope is authorized for this publication. Do not add `workflow` or `delete:packages`, expose the token, or omit the follow-up to remove `repo`.

- Verify with GHCR and GitHub APIs that `latest` and the new `0.0.n` share one digest. Confirm documented Compose access; if package visibility needs a one-way public change, report the explicit user action instead of changing it.
- Keep Compose on GHCR `latest` while retaining local builds.

[package]
name = "agent-sandbox"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.85"
description = "Containerized code sandbox service"
license = "MIT"
publish = false

[dependencies]
futures-util = "0.3"
object_store = { version = "0.12", features = ["aws"] }
prost = "0.13"
tokio = { version = "1.44", features = [
  "fs",
  "macros",
  "process",
  "rt-multi-thread",
  "signal",
  "time",
] }
tonic = "0.12"
tonic-health = "0.12"
tonic-reflection = "0.12"
tracing = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = "0.3"
walkdir = "2"

[build-dependencies]
tonic-build = "0.12"

[dev-dependencies]
tempfile = "3"

[lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"

[lints.clippy]
all = "deny"
pedantic = "deny"

services:
  agent:
    build:
      context: .
    image: ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest
    environment:
      AGENT_SANDBOX_LISTEN: 0.0.0.0:8080
      AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_BUCKET: ${AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_BUCKET:-}
      AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_ENDPOINT: ${AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_ENDPOINT:-}
      AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_PREFIX: ${AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_PREFIX:-home}
      AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}
      AWS_ALLOW_HTTP: ${AWS_ALLOW_HTTP:-false}
      AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: ${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION:-us-east-1}
      AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    restart: unless-stopped
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python
        - -c
        - "import socket; socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 8080), timeout=2).close()"
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 2s

content.text:
# Agent sandbox

Agent sandbox is a Nix-built container service for running coding-agent workloads as an unprivileged user. This bootstrap provides the Rust service package, OCI image, rootless Podman environment, Docker Compose compatibility, and an ephemeral `systemd-nspawn` runner.

The service exposes the versioned API in [`proto/v0`](proto/v0), gRPC reflection, and the standard gRPC health service on port 8080. Filesystem calls read and write small files under `/home/user`; command calls start a fresh process and return its standard output, standard error, and exit code. Paths that escape `/home/user`, including symlink escapes, are rejected.

## Set up

Install Nix with flakes enabled. Enter the development environment:

```console
nix develop
```

The first shell activation after each reboot asks for wheel authorization. It installs a cgroup delegation drop-in under `/run`, then starts a rootless, Docker-compatible Podman API as the transient `agent-sandbox-podman.service` user unit. The service lasts for the user session; neither the drop-in nor its marker survives a reboot. Set `AGENT_SANDBOX_SKIP_PODMAN_SERVICE=1` on hosts where service startup is not wanted.

With nix-direnv installed, `direnv allow` activates the same shell when entering the repository. The shell includes Cargo, Clippy, rustfmt, Podman, and podman-compose and exports `DOCKER_HOST` and `DOCKER_SOCK` for the rootless Podman socket.

## Build and check

```console
nix fmt
nix flake check --print-build-logs
nix build .#agent-sandbox
nix build .#agent-image
```

Run the Docker-in-NixOS integration test explicitly:

```console
nix build .#nixos-vm-test -L
```

The VM starts `docker.service` and a host SeaweedFS S3 service, loads the Nix-built image, and starts the single Compose container. Host-side `grpcurl` calls test file access, path confinement, command failures, and all three acceptance scripts. The test also verifies startup and graceful-shutdown synchronization against the host S3 service.

The root flake follows the consumer-clean structure from `nix-project-template`: package and image definitions live under `nix/flake/`, while formatters, hooks, and shell tools are isolated in `dev/`.

## Run containers

Load the Nix-built OCI archive into Podman:

```console
podman load < "$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths .#agent-image)"
podman run --rm --publish 8080:8080 ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest
```

The compatibility Dockerfile and Compose definition run through rootless Podman:

```console
podman-compose up --build
podman-compose down
```

Both images run as `sandbox-manager`, use `/home/user` as the home and working directory, preinstall every library declared in `pyproject.toml`, and start `agent-sandbox` as their entrypoint. Compose references `ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest`; `--build` replaces it locally with the compatibility Dockerfile build.

## Call the service

Reflection lets `grpcurl` call the service without local descriptor files:

```console
grpcurl -plaintext 127.0.0.1:8080 list sandbox.v0.FilesystemService
grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"path":"notes.txt","content":"aGVsbG8="}' \
  127.0.0.1:8080 sandbox.v0.FilesystemService/WriteFile
grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"argv":["python","-c","print(6 * 7)"]}' \
  127.0.0.1:8080 sandbox.v0.CommandService/ExecuteCommand
```

Protocol Buffer `bytes` fields use base64 in JSON. `ExecuteCommand.argv` bypasses the shell; request a shell explicitly when shell syntax is needed. The optional working directory is relative to `/home/user`, and command timeouts default to 30 seconds with a five-minute maximum.

## Configure S3 synchronization

Set `AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_BUCKET` to enable persistence. The service downloads the configured prefix before accepting requests and uploads `/home/user` after `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`. These variables configure the store:

- `AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_BUCKET`: bucket name; an empty value disables persistence.
- `AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_PREFIX`: object prefix, defaulting to `home`.
- `AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_ENDPOINT`: optional S3-compatible endpoint for services such as MinIO.
- Standard `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` variables provide credentials and region. Set `AWS_ALLOW_HTTP=true` for a plain-HTTP local endpoint.

Compose passes these variables into its single container and maps `host.docker.internal` to the host gateway, so a host S3-compatible service can be used without adding another Compose service.

## Continuous integration

GitHub Actions remains a check-only adapter. SourceHut runs the same `nix flake check --print-build-logs` contract from [`.build.yml`](.build.yml), builds the Nix OCI archive, and publishes only `refs/heads/main` to GHCR. Other SourceHut branches build and test the image but cannot publish it. The NixOS VM test is a package, not a flake check, so neither CI system builds or runs it.

The SourceHut repository is the registered private mirror at `git.sr.ht/~fuzzybear3965/agent-sandbox`. A push containing `.build.yml` submits a build automatically. The manifest uses the existing SourceHut CI SSH-key secret to clone this private repository.

### GHCR secret

Create a GitHub personal access token (classic) for `johnrichardrinehart` at <https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=write:packages>. This URL avoids the GitHub token form's default addition of the broad `repo` scope. Keep only `write:packages`, which includes image download and upload; do not add `repo`, `workflow`, or `delete:packages`.

The SourceHut file secret declared in `.build.yml` is mounted at `~/.ghcr_pat`; its complete contents are the token. SourceHut runs tasks with shell tracing enabled, so the publishing app reads the file with tracing disabled and passes the token to `skopeo login` through standard input.

A main build publishes `ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest` and `0.0.n`, where `n` is the main commit count, then confirms that both tags have the same digest. GHCR makes a new personal package private by default. After its first publication, change the package visibility to public in its GitHub package settings so the documented Compose command can pull it without authentication.

## Run with systemd-nspawn

```console
nix run .#agent-systemd-nspawn
```

This command asks for wheel authorization and launches the Nix root filesystem through `systemd-nspawn` with an ephemeral overlay. It runs the service as `sandbox-manager`; changes vanish when the unit exits. Inspect the generated command without elevation with:

```console
nix run .#agent-systemd-nspawn -- --dry-run
```

commit 7005437229ba91d43a30e4e350703bbe032fb19b
Author: John Rinehart <johnrichardrinehart@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Aug 6 13:44:06 2026 -0400

    rpc: stub versioned gRPC services
    
    Replace the temporary HTTP health endpoint with versioned filesystem,
    command, and health APIs. Generate bindings in the build directory and
    expose reflection plus standard gRPC health reporting.
    
    Add an explicit Docker-backed NixOS VM package that verifies service
    readiness with grpcurl. Keep it outside flake checks so CI does not run
    the expensive VM.

+

+
+## Lint exceptions
+

# Agent sandbox

Agent sandbox is a Nix-built container service for running coding-agent workloads as an unprivileged user. This bootstrap provides the Rust service package, OCI image, rootless Podman environment, Docker Compose compatibility, and an ephemeral `systemd-nspawn` runner.

The service exposes the versioned API in [`proto/v0`](proto/v0), gRPC reflection, and the standard gRPC health service on port 8080. Filesystem calls read and write small files under `/home/user`; command calls start a fresh process and return its standard output, standard error, and exit code. Paths that escape `/home/user`, including symlink escapes, are rejected.

## Set up

Install Nix with flakes enabled. Enter the development environment:

```console
nix develop
```

The shell provides two separate container runtimes. `podman` runs rootless without setup or authorization. The `docker` client connects to a project-local Docker daemon started directly by the shell, not by a systemd unit. Starting that rootful daemon asks for wheel authorization. Its socket, process files, and storage live under `/run/user/$UID/agent-sandbox-docker-$PID` and are removed when the development shell exits.

With nix-direnv installed, `direnv allow` activates the same environment when entering the repository. Each interactive shell gets its own Docker daemon; leaving the repository or closing that shell stops it. The shell exports `DOCKER_HOST` and `DOCKER_SOCK` for its Docker socket. Set `AGENT_SANDBOX_SKIP_DOCKER_DAEMON=1` when only rootless Podman is needed.

## Build and check

```console
nix fmt
nix flake check --print-build-logs
nix build .#agent-sandbox
nix build .#agent-image
```

Run the Docker-in-NixOS integration test explicitly:

```console
nix build .#nixos-vm-test -L
```

The VM starts `docker.service` and a host SeaweedFS S3 service, loads the Nix-built image, and starts the single Compose container. Host-side `grpcurl` calls test file access, path confinement, command failures, and all three acceptance scripts. The test also verifies startup and graceful-shutdown synchronization against the host S3 service.

The root flake follows the consumer-clean structure from `nix-project-template`: package and image definitions live under `nix/flake/`, while formatters, hooks, and shell tools are isolated in `dev/`.

## Run containers

Load the Nix-built OCI archive into either runtime:

```console
podman load < "$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths .#agent-image)"
podman run --rm --publish 8080:8080 ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest

# Or use the shell's ephemeral Docker daemon.
docker load < "$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths .#agent-image)"
docker run --rm --publish 8080:8080 ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest
```

The compatibility Dockerfile and Compose definition run through rootless Podman:

```console
podman-compose up --build
podman-compose down
```

## Call the service

Reflection lets `grpcurl` call the service without local descriptor files:

```console
grpcurl -plaintext 127.0.0.1:8080 list sandbox.v0.FilesystemService
grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"path":"notes.txt","content":"aGVsbG8="}' \
  127.0.0.1:8080 sandbox.v0.FilesystemService/WriteFile
grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"argv":["python","-c","print(6 * 7)"]}' \
  127.0.0.1:8080 sandbox.v0.CommandService/ExecuteCommand
```

Protocol Buffer `bytes` fields use base64 in JSON. `ExecuteCommand.argv` bypasses the shell; request a shell explicitly when shell syntax is needed. The optional working directory is relative to `/home/user`, and command timeouts default to 30 seconds with a five-minute maximum.

## Configure S3 synchronization

Set `AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_BUCKET` to enable persistence. The service downloads the configured prefix before accepting requests and uploads `/home/user` after `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`. These variables configure the store:

- `AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_BUCKET`: bucket name; an empty value disables persistence.
- `AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_PREFIX`: object prefix, defaulting to `home`.
- `AGENT_SANDBOX_S3_ENDPOINT`: optional S3-compatible endpoint for services such as MinIO.
- Standard `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` variables provide credentials and region. Set `AWS_ALLOW_HTTP=true` for a plain-HTTP local endpoint or `AWS_SKIP_SIGNATURE=true` for an anonymous test service.

Compose passes these variables into its single container and maps `host.docker.internal` to the host gateway, so a host S3-compatible service can be used without adding another Compose service.

## Continuous integration

GitHub Actions remains a check-only adapter. SourceHut runs the same `nix flake check --print-build-logs` contract from [`.build.yml`](.build.yml), builds the Nix OCI archive, and publishes only `refs/heads/main` to GHCR. Other SourceHut branches build and test the image but cannot publish it. The NixOS VM test is a package, not a flake check, so neither CI system builds or runs it.

The SourceHut repository is the registered private mirror at `git.sr.ht/~fuzzybear3965/agent-sandbox`. A push containing `.build.yml` submits a build automatically. The manifest uses the existing SourceHut CI SSH-key secret to clone this private repository.

### GHCR secret

Create a GitHub personal access token (classic) for `johnrichardrinehart` at <https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=write:packages>. This URL avoids the GitHub token form's default addition of the broad `repo` scope. Keep only `write:packages`, which includes image download and upload; do not add `repo`, `workflow`, or `delete:packages`.

The SourceHut file secret declared in `.build.yml` is mounted at `~/.ghcr_pat`; its complete contents are the token. SourceHut runs tasks with shell tracing enabled, so the publishing app reads the file with tracing disabled and passes the token to `skopeo login` through standard input.

A main build publishes `ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest` and `0.0.n`, where `n` is the main commit count, then confirms that both tags have the same digest. GHCR makes a new personal package private by default. After its first publication, change the package visibility to public in its GitHub package settings so the documented Compose command can pull it without authentication.

## Run with systemd-nspawn

```console
nix run .#agent-systemd-nspawn
```

This command asks for wheel authorization and launches the Nix root filesystem through `systemd-nspawn` with an ephemeral overlay. It runs the service as `sandbox-manager`; changes vanish when the unit exits. Inspect the generated command without elevation with:

```console
nix run .#agent-systemd-nspawn -- --dry-run
```

edits.oldText:
The shell provides two separate container runtimes. `podman` runs rootless without setup or authorization. The `docker` client connects to a project-local Docker daemon started directly by the shell, not by a systemd unit. Starting that rootful daemon asks for wheel authorization. Its socket, process files, and storage live under `/run/user/$UID/agent-sandbox-docker-$PID` and are removed when the development shell exits.

With nix-direnv installed, `direnv allow` activates the same environment when entering the repository. Each interactive shell gets its own Docker daemon; leaving the repository or closing that shell stops it. The shell exports `DOCKER_HOST` and `DOCKER_SOCK` for its Docker socket. Set `AGENT_SANDBOX_SKIP_DOCKER_DAEMON=1` when only rootless Podman is needed.
edits.newText:
The shell provides two separate container runtimes. On first activation after each reboot, it asks for wheel authorization to install an ephemeral cgroup delegation drop-in under `/run`, then starts the session-long rootless `agent-sandbox-podman.service` with a Docker-compatible socket. The `docker` client uses a separate project-local Docker daemon started directly by the shell. Its socket, process files, storage, and isolated bridge live under `/run/user/$UID` and are removed when the development shell exits.

With nix-direnv installed, `direnv allow` activates the same environment when entering the repository. Each interactive shell gets its own Docker daemon; leaving the repository or closing that shell stops it. The shell exports `DOCKER_HOST` and `DOCKER_SOCK` for Docker plus `PODMAN_DOCKER_HOST` and `PODMAN_DOCKER_SOCK` for Podman. Set `AGENT_SANDBOX_SKIP_DOCKER_DAEMON=1` to skip Docker or `AGENT_SANDBOX_SKIP_PODMAN_SERVICE=1` to skip the Podman API service.
